extra.message: The `expr` query parameter of GET /ops/formula/seller-cast-255 is passed directly to eval(). Removing __builtins__ does not sandbox Python eval: attribute-chain escapes (e.g. ().__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()) allow arbitrary code execution. The only protection is the shared static _wrk_gate token; anyone holding it gets remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: In GET /ops/shell/seller-probe-396 the user-controlled `host` query parameter is concatenated unsanitized into a shell command passed to _os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). Shell metacharacters (;, |, &, `, $()) allow arbitrary OS command execution with the application's privileges.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: In POST /ops/dock/seller-dropbin-slot-022 the user-controlled `packet_ref` query parameter is joined to the incoming directory (incoming_dir / packet_ref) and the raw request body is written with target.write_bytes(). There is no traversal check, so '../' sequences escape the directory and allow arbitrary file write/overwrite anywhere the process can write (e.g. overwriting source or config files to achieve code execution).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: In POST /ops/dock/seller-shelf-394 the user-controlled `name` query parameter is used directly as BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name and the full request body is written via target.write_bytes(body) with no validation. A `name` containing '../' permits arbitrary file write outside the export directory, including overwriting application files.

extra.message: In POST /ops/mongo/seller-lane-416 the attacker-supplied JSON body (payload.get("filter", payload)) is passed directly as the MongoDB filter to MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query). The attacker controls the entire query document and can inject MongoDB operators ($ne, $regex, $where) to extract arbitrary records or execute server-side JavaScript where $where is enabled.

extra.message: In GET /ops/badge/seller-gate-436 the elevated-access decision is based solely on the client-controlled ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge header (badge == "lead"). Any client can trivially set these values to obtain the elevated lane/payroll/casework response; the authorization decision trusts client-supplied data with no server-side verification.

extra.message: The default secret_key ('change-me-in-production-please-this-is-a-dev-default-key') is hardcoded and is used to sign/verify all session JWTs (security.py create_session_token/decode_session_token) and to HMAC API keys and password-reset tokens (hash_token). A deployment that does not override this public default allows anyone to forge valid session tokens (including admin) and reset-token hashes, bypassing all authentication.

extra.message: In GET /ops/blurb/seller-tile-321 the user-controlled `card` query parameter is rendered through Jinja2 Template("{{ card|safe }}") and returned as an HTMLResponse. The |safe filter disables auto-escaping, so any HTML/JavaScript in `card` is served unescaped — reflected XSS whenever this response is rendered by a browser.

extra.message: In GET /ops/origin/seller-mirror-376 the Origin request header is echoed verbatim into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. Any origin can therefore make credentialed cross-origin requests, allowing a malicious site to read responses and act on behalf of an authenticated victim.

extra.message: Unlike every other route in this module, GET /ops/fold/seller-margin-fold-024 has no Depends(_wrk_gate) or any other authentication dependency (its signature is only (fold_ref: str = "latest")). extra.message: In GET /ops/spool/seller-fan-305 the `count` query parameter has no upper bound and directly sizes a list comprehension ([{"idx": idx, "ref": ref} for idx in range(count)]). extra.message: POST /api/auth/password-reset/request returns the raw reset token in the response body when settings.environment == "development" — and "development" is the default value of Settings.environment in config.py. If the environment is left at the default in a real deployment, anyone who requests a reset for a victim's email receives the token and can take over the account via /password-reset/confirm.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: POST /api/auth/register returns 409 'Email already registered' when the submitted email exists, disclosing which email addresses have accounts. (Login uses a constant message, but registration does not.) This enables systematic account enumeration for targeted attacks.

cwe: CWE-204: Observable Response Discrepancy

extra.message: The authentication endpoints (login, register, password-reset request/confirm) implement no rate limiting, account lockout, or CAPTCHA. An attacker can make unlimited attempts to brute-force passwords or flood password-reset token creation without throttling.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: _validate_url only checks that the vendor-supplied webhook target_url starts with http:// or https://; there is no blocklist for private, loopback, or link-local ranges (127.0.0.1, 10.x, 169.254.169.254 cloud metadata). Any component that delivers these webhooks would let a vendor direct server-side requests at internal services. (The current code records deliveries without performing the HTTP call, so exploitation depends on the delivery path.)

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: The Webhook.secret column stores the webhook signing secret as a plaintext String(128) in the database. Any database read (backup leak, injection, DBA access) exposes all signing secrets, enabling forgery of webhook payloads. Secrets should be stored hashed or encrypted, as API keys are.
